Diego / Monica —

I've reviewed HealthSync's annotated redlines. High level: their asks are reasonable but a few items need careful wording to avoid opening our standard escape clauses. I've attached a tracked redline and an SCCs matrix that maps their requested changes to our positions.

Key points to address in the redline:
- Controller vs Processor: Keep our standard processor obligations but accept a clarified data processing schedule that lists HealthSync as controller for Customer Data. We should avoid prescriptive obligations about their downstream controllers.
- SCCs insertion: We can incorporate the SCCs by reference but we should retain a short operational carveout that allows for automatic fallback to the latest SCCs via an addendum (language included in the attached doc).
- KMS: For standard SaaS customers we offer Redwood-managed keys with contractual encryption at rest and in-transit protections. For customers requiring CMK (customer-managed keys) at rest, we handle as a Private deployment add-on; that will require a dedicated infra review and pricing change.
- Routing: Provide contractual language that EU-region routing is the default and that we publish any cross-border exceptions in our Order Form exhibit. We cannot guarantee absolute physical-only exclusion without a Private deployment.

Procurement ask: If HealthSync needs CMK or strict physical-only EU tenancy, we need to route to Solutions + Pricing for a Dedicated/Private quote. That will likely push the procurement gate beyond 05/28.

Next steps (I'll do these today):
1) Attach: DPA_redline_20260521.docx (suggested tracked changes)
2) Attach: SCCs_matrix.xlsx (mapping + recommended language)
3) Draft a one-page cover note for the evidence pack summarizing where we are aligned and where we need procurement/solutions decisions.

I'll upload artifacts to the drive folder and share the link once complete.

—Marissa
Deputy GC, Contracts & Privacy
